entities.summary: John Milton Bigelow was an American physician and botanist. He had a successful medical practice, and also, a keen interest in botany - especially native plants with medical applications. He participated as a botanist and surgeon on two important expeditions through the American Southwest—the Mexican Boundary Survey and the 35th Parallel Expedition for the Pacific Railroad Surveys. He also amassed a significant collection of California plants that yielded many new species. He communicated his botanical results with the three top American botanists of the day, John Torrey, Asa Gray, and George Engelmann.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: John Milton Bigelow's expeditions and botanical discoveries contributed significantly to the understanding of California's flora, with his collection yielding many new species. His work had a lasting impact on American botany.
